articles.title: Arsenal: Former Man Utd defender Ona Batlle joins Gunners on a permanent deal from Barcelona
articles.summary: Ona Batlle re-joined Barcelona in 2023 following a spell with Manchester United; World Cup winner signs permanent deal with Arsenal, came second in last season's WSL behind runaway champions Manchester City
articles.body:
The 27-year-old joins the north London side on a permanent contract of undisclosed length.

Batlle had re-joined Barca - the club where she started her career - in the summer of 2023 after her contract at Man Utd expired.

Across three seasons back in Spain, she made 114 appearances and scored 14 goals.

"I'm very happy and excited to get going," she said after the completion of her move to Arsenal.

"Arsenal is one of the biggest clubs in the world, and I can't wait to feel the joy of playing in front of our supporters at Emirates Stadium alongside so many great players.

"I want to win trophies and I feel this is the right place to achieve that."

Gunners head coach Renee Slegers added: "I'm delighted that we've been able to bring Ona to the club.

"She's a hugely experienced full-back with strong attacking intent and great physical attributes. She's a winner and we want to go for more wins together."

Batlle spent three years with Man Utd and was part of the squad that finished as runners-up in the 2022/23 FA Cup.

She has 76 senior caps for Spain to her name and won the World Cup with La Roja in 2023.

Arsenal beating their rivals in the transfer market

"It has been quite the busy summer so far for Arsenal as they look to evolve their squad. There have been high-profile outgoings with the likes of Beth Mead, Katie McCabe leaving, as well as Victoria Pelova and Laia Codina - perhaps not household names but no less important.

"The reality is the teams around them will only be getting stronger. Manchester City will want more depth as they add European football back to their calendar, while Chelsea are a wounded animal after a poor season by their high standards - so much so, McCabe joined them after leaving the Gunners.

"Tottenham have already made a string of impressive signings while Manchester United too will be disappointed to have dropped away from the top three race so easily.

"But Arsenal are arguably leading the way among all of these clubs in terms of transfers.

"Batlle comes with bags of experience both in the WSL with Man Utd and Europe, as does Georgia Stanway - the Lionesses star who has arrived from Bayern Munich.

"Then there is a double arrival from the Bundesliga - Geraldine Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt and Selina Cerci from Hoffenheim. The question for those two is how quickly they can adapt to WSL football? Arsenal have begun slowly over the past two years and will not want another this season.

"What is interesting - and perhaps unsurprisingly - is all four of these players are 26 or 27 years old. They are entering their prime years, while also having plenty of experience elsewhere.

"It's clear which direction Arsenal's transfer strategy is heading and so far, it is being executed flawlessly."

articles.title: WSL transfer latest: Barcelona closing in on deal for Man City forward Kerolin in move worth £1.28m
articles.summary: Barcelona are set to break their transfer record as they close in on signing Man City forward Kerolin; the deal is set to be worth £1.28m; it would represent the largest fee ever received by a WSL club, eclipsing Olivia Smith's £1m move to Arsenal from Liverpool last summer
articles.body:
The deal would represent the largest fee ever received by a WSL club, eclipsing Olivia Smith's £1m move to Arsenal from Liverpool last summer.

Kerolin only joined City in January last year and had another two years left on her contract, but Barca are sufficiently determined to sign her to smash their own transfer record by more than 200 per cent.

Their previous most expensive transfer was then-Man City midfielder Keira Walsh , who joined in 2022 for a fee of €470,000 (£400,000).

The Spanish champions have already lost forward Salma Paralluelo this summer.

Kerolin scored nine goals in 15 WSL games for City last season to help them to their first WSL title since 2016.

Barcelona biting back after stars swap Catalonia for WSL

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Callum Bishop:

Just months after Barcelona secured their European dominance yet again by winning all four major trophies available to them, including the Champions League, Barcelona watched their core being dismantled.

Two-time Ballon d'Or Feminin winner Alexia Putellas was the headline departure, but she was joined by Mapi Leon in moves to London City Lionesses.

There was also defender Ona Batlle, who opted to join Arsenal. It is a big sign that the appeal of the WSL is growing and threatening to upset the apple cart in Catalonia.

However, the move for Kerolin is a statement of intent from Barcelona. They are the superpower in women's football and, despite losing many of their stars, they still retain their own allure.

In targeting the Brazilian, Barcelona are looking to add some potency in attack. On the surface, Kerolin's nine WSL goals last season may not blow you away. Team-mates Khadija Shaw (21) and Vivianne Miedema (10) both managed more.

However, Kerolin's per-90 stats show just how potent she is. She ranked fifth in goals, second in assists and fourth in big chances converted. Had it not been for an injury she suffered in October, her numbers would no doubt have been more impressive. But the per-90 conversion shows just how important she was in City's title charge and the calibre of player Barcelona would be getting.

articles.title: Hannah Hampton: Chelsea goalkeeper signs new two-year contract to extend stay at Stamford Bridge
articles.summary: Hannah Hampton has signed a new two-year deal at Chelsea; the England international's contract had expired at the end of June, technically rendering her a free agent; the confirmation ends any speculation over an exit this summer
articles.body:
Hampton's contract had expired at the end of June, making her a free agent, but the 25-year-old has now agreed to extend her stay.

Since signing for the Blues from Aston Villa in 2023, Hampton has won five trophies, as well as helping England to retain their European Championship crown last summer.

She also won the Yashin Trophy at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in 2025, recognising her among the best goalkeepers in the world.

"I'm really happy," Hampton said. "Chelsea have always been my dream club to play for in England so to be able to extend for another two years is a proud moment.

"When I moved to London from the Midlands, it was my first time moving away from home and everyone at Chelsea made it feel like a home away from home and somewhere I have been able to grow not only as a player but as a person.

"I don't want that journey to stop and I want to continue to grow more and learn more as a person.

"I know there is so much more I can achieve and so much more as a team we can achieve. I am going to do everything I can to help Chelsea get back to being as successful as we have been in the past."

Hampton kept seven clean sheets for Chelsea last season, the joint-most in the Women's Super League, as Sonia Bompastor's side finished third behind Arsenal and champions Man City.

She played a pivotal role in the Blues' domestic treble campaign the year before and won the Golden Glove award in consecutive years.

Analysis: Hampton's deal important for stability at changeable Chelsea

Chelsea's period of flux has coincided with plenty of big-name, high-profile players exiting the club. Uncertainty over Hannah Hampton's future pointed towards her being next. But finally, the news of a deal will be welcomed by fans.

Hampton isn't the sort Chelsea could afford to lose. Her quality has never been called into question and she remains the perfect age and profile of goalkeeper to continue to thrive at the WSL's most successful club.

Clearly the burden of last year's trophy failure has weighed heavy on those who have been around the place a while. "Get back to being successful" was the line that struck me most from Hampton's comments on why she's re-signed.

It'll be interesting to understand what is defined as success at Chelsea next season. Essentially, how the goalposts might have changed after such a humbling year, knocked off their perch by Man City and overtaken by Arsenal, too. It will not be an easy task to wrestle back initiative.

Nevertheless, Hampton's signature is a big tick in the box and clears up any doubt about her position being under threat.

articles.summary: Women's Super League 2026/27 fixtures announced; season begins on Friday September 4 as London City Lionesses host Man Utd; champions Man City host Birmingham City on opening weekend; WSL expanded from 12 to 14 teams with Birmingham, Crystal Palace and Charlton Athletic promoted
articles.body:
The fixtures for the upcoming campaign have been released, with kick-off times and broadcast picks confirmed for the first four weekends, featuring more matches than ever after the league expanded from 12 teams to 14 after Birmingham City, Crystal Palace and Charlton Athletic secured promotion from WSL 2.

Sky Sports will show 90 per cent of all WSL matches live on Sky Sports and NOW - 163 matches in total, as well as the play-off - with selected games also shown on the Sky Sports WSL YouTube channel. There will be greater flexibility over fixtures, with fewer matches kicking off at the same time.

London City , who signed two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas this summer, will launch the new season in front of the Sky Sports cameras on Friday September 4 against Man Utd before champions Man City host newcomers Birmingham City on a bumper day of action on Sunday September 6 featuring five live games.

The other matches on the first Sunday of the season see last year's runners-up Arsenal start with a trip to Brighton , while Tottenham host a London derby against West Ham , Liverpool visit newly-promoted Charlton and Crystal Palace , who secured an immediate return to the top flight, face Everton .

Eight-time winners Chelsea host Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge on Saturday September 5.

Man Utd face a difficult start to the season with their second game coming at home to Chelsea on Sunday September 13 before they head to the Emirates Stadium to play Arsenal on Saturday September 19, with both matches live on Sky Sports. Arsenal also host Chelsea on Sunday September 27, live on Sky Sports.

The first Merseyside derby of the season sees Everton travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday September 27, live on Sky Sports.

Relegation remains in place following the expansion to the league, with the last-placed team automatically relegated, and the 13th-placed side facing a play-off with the WSL 2 runners-up.

articles.title: Kerolin Nicoli transfer news: Man City forward joins Barcelona as Women's Super League's most expensive export
articles.summary: Brazilian forward Kerolin was schooled on the streets of Sao Paulo, playing barefoot with boys; now, she has signed for European giants Barcelona from Man City; her fee is the highest ever received for a Women's Super League player
articles.body:
Kerolin's £1.25m fee breaks record held by Olivia Smith's sale from Liverpool to Arsenal last summer. Barcelona were willing to smash their own transfer policy in pursuit of the Brazilian, too, having never previously paid a fee over £500k.

But Kerolin represents an exception to the rule. It's always been that way, from the start of her journey playing barefoot with boys on the streets of Sao Paulo. She was different. The ball hurt to kick, she confessed, but she did it anyway.

As such, there is perhaps an air of inevitability about the 26-year-old's switch to the four-time European champions. This is the path she expected to follow. "Always the most highly-ranked players are playing here or in Spain," she told Sky Sports upon signing for Man City in January 2025. "To be in the vision of the world."

Being considered among the game's most elite does not necessitate playing for Barcelona, but it helps. Each of the last five Ballon d'Or recipients were representing the Catalonia club at the time of winning the prize. Kerolin is now the team-mate of its current holder Aitana Bonmati.

Indeed, if Ballon d'Or is the mission Barcelona has proven the means. It's fertile ground for notoriety and success, with silverware almost guaranteed and the chance to star in a team undergoing reinvention under Pere Romeu. A summer of change has seen plenty of big names leave: Alexia Putellas, Ona Batlle and Mapi Leon among them.

But the turning point for Kerolin follows the departure of forward Salma Paralluelo, a player similar in profile to her. The 22-year-old scored twice in last season's Champions League final, a precocious young talent with a huge appetite for success, now clubless after failing to agree terms.

Kerolin, who once held transfer interest from Arsenal, is perfectly poised to succeed her. Barcelona's need for a player of Kerolin's talents is greater than that of City's, flush with versatile wingers, while the considerable fee sends a well-timed message.

Maintenance as Europe's leading superpower does not come cheap. Barcelona have been burdened by financial constraints over the past few years, reliant on their global pull to attract and retain the game's top stars. But others have caught up; no longer is their lure enough in isolation.

To keep pace, Barcelona must show willing to be as financially front-footed as their European rivals. Kerolin's capture is a statement signing for a side in need of some validation after bidding farewell to four high-profile players in as many weeks. Proof that Romeu is remodelling, rather than revolutionising his team of aces.

Nor is this move an ego trip. Kerolin made 26 WSL appearances for Man City, scoring 12 goals. Only Khadija Shaw and Stina Blackstenius have a better goals-per-90 ratio during that time. No player can match Kerolin for take-ons attempted or completed.

In fact, very few forwards boast her complete skillset. She can balance scoring with creating, on-the-ball craft with off-the-ball industry, and has explosive speed in both directions. She scores screamers, too, with quality off both flanks.

Her departure less than two years after signing will feel premature for many in Manchester, not least City's leading scorer Shaw, for whom she made a habit of assisting.

But business is business; a rare deal where the benefits are mutually divided. Man City reap significant return on their investment and make space for one of their other wide forwards to make strides. Any one of Aoba Fujino, Mary Fowler, Iman Beney, or newly-recruited Beth Mead would fit the bill.

Barcelona, meanwhile, have a growing awareness of the increased competition they face to stay queens of Europe. They remain the highest benchmark for success for now, but need fresh impetus to stay there. Kerolin greatly enhances their chances.

articles.title: Ghislain Konan: Wolves announce signing of Ivory Coast defender
articles.summary: Wolves announce the signing of Portugal-based defender Ghislain Konan.
articles.body:
Wolves have announced their final signing of the summer transfer window - almost 23 hours after it closed - by bringing in Portugal-based Ivory Coast defender Ghislain Konan.

The 30-year-old 57-times capped left-back, who played under new Wolves head coach Cesar Peixoto at Gil Vicente in the Portuguese Liga last season, has signed on a one-year deal.

He fills the gap in the squad left by David Moller Wolfe's departure to SV Hamburg on deadline day.

Konan started his career with Ivorian club ASEC Mimosas before moving to Portugal with Vitoria Guimaraes.

He then moved in 2018 to Stade de Reims, where he spent five years, before a stint in the Saudi Pro League, first at Al-Nassr, then Al-Fayha, half a season with Spanish second tier side Burgos and then last season's time with Gil Vicente.

articles.title: Messi’s iconic No.10 successor revealed as 21-year-old star set to inherit legendary shirt if one condition is met
articles.summary: Football News: Lionel Messi's retirement leaves a legacy as Argentina's No.10, with 21-year-old Nico Paz emerging as the successor if coach Scaloni signs a new deal. Discover the significance of this pivotal shirt and Paz's potential in the post-Messi era.
articles.body: Lionel Messi's retirement from international football has left Argentina with one of the most difficult shirts in world football to fill. The No.10 has belonged to Messi for years after previously carrying the legacy of Diego Maradona, and the player reportedly chosen to inherit it is one of Argentina's brightest young talents. Nico Paz has emerged as the reported successor to the iconic shirt, but there is one important condition attached to the plan.Nico Paz reportedly chosen to inherit Messi's No.10According to ESPN Argentina, Argentina have already identified Paz as the player they want to hand Messi's No.10 shirt to, although the decision is tied to Scaloni's future with the national team.The 21-year-old attacking midfielder has previously worn No.18 during his 11 appearances for Argentina, but he could now take on the number associated with two of the country's greatest-ever footballers.ESPN Argentina insider Federico Bueno reported that the plan has already been decided internally and is being taken seriously."If Scaloni renews as Argentina's coach, which is expected to be negotiated in the coming months, the No. 10 shirt will go to Nico Paz. This has already been decided internally and is being taken very seriously," Bueno said.That means Paz's succession of Messi is not yet unconditional. Scaloni's contract situation must first be resolved, with the 48-year-old expected to negotiate a new deal in the coming months.Scaloni has been Argentina's head coach since 2018 and oversaw the side's run to the 2022 World Cup title in Qatar before taking them to the 2026 World Cup final. If he agrees to continue in the role, Paz is reportedly set to become the next No.10.Why Paz has emerged as the choiceThere are more established names within the Argentina squad who could have been considered for such an iconic shirt, including Enzo Fernandez and Alexis Mac Allister, but the reported succession plan points towards Paz as the player viewed as capable of leading the next generation.Paz, 21, was born in Spain but is the son of former Argentina international Pablo Paz. He came through the Real Madrid academy and made eight first-team appearances for the Spanish giants before leaving for Italian club Como in 2024.His development in Serie A has accelerated under former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas, with Paz establishing himself as one of the most exciting young attacking players in European football.He has made 77 appearances in all competitions for Como, scoring 19 goals, while his performances have repeatedly fuelled speculation that Real Madrid could bring him back to the Bernabeu.A return to Madrid has reportedly been tipped in virtually every transfer window since his departure, underlining how highly the Spanish club continues to regard the player it developed.For Argentina, however, his development has taken on a different significance.Paz has already earned 11 senior caps and is now being considered for a role that carries considerably more weight than simply becoming another attacking option in the squad.Messi leaves behind an enormous legacyWhoever takes the No.10 will inevitably be compared with Messi, even if Argentina's next generation has no realistic way of reproducing what the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner achieved.Messi departs the national team as a former world champion, having captained Argentina to glory in Qatar in 2022, and as the country's long-standing No.10 and leader.He leaves after 207 international appearances, having built a legacy that also places him as the second-highest goalscorer in World Cup history.His decision came after Argentina's defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final in New Jersey, with Messi making clear that he felt his international journey had reached its natural conclusion."It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts deep down – but I understand that the time has come," Messi said in his retirement statement."I swear to you that I always gave it my all – not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football.""Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team.""I’ve given everything I had; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up who deserve to be here."A huge shirt for Argentina's next generationThe significance of the No.10 means Paz would not simply be inheriting a squad number.Argentina's shirt has already carried the weight of Diego Maradona, who famously wore it during his World Cup-winning campaign in 1986, before Messi created his own extraordinary chapter in the number.That makes the decision to give it to a 21-year-old a significant statement about how Argentina view Paz's potential.The Como playmaker is still at an early stage of his international career, with only 11 appearances to his name, and he has never been expected to simply replace Messi as a player. Instead, the reported decision reflects the belief that he can become one of the central figures in Argentina's post-Messi era.There is still one hurdle before that succession can happen.Scaloni's future must first be settled. If the World Cup-winning coach agrees a new contract, the reported plan is for Paz to move from the No.18 he has worn during his early international career into Messi's iconic No.10.For now, that remains a reported internal decision rather than an officially confirmed shirt change. But if Scaloni stays, Paz appears set to become the young Argentine entrusted with carrying the most famous number in the country's football history into its next era.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Argentina can't retire Messi's legendary No.10 because of the same FIFA rule that stopped them honouring Maradona in 2002
articles.summary: Football News: Argentina faces a FIFA regulation barrier that stops them from retiring Lionel Messi's iconic No.10 shirt, similar to the case with Diego Maradona in 2002, as the legacy of both football legends looms large.
articles.body: Lionel Messi’s retirement from international football has left Argentina with a question that feels almost impossible to answer: what happens to the No.10 shirt now? For many supporters, the obvious answer is to retire it forever. Messi wore it for two decades, became Argentina’s most-capped player and all-time leading scorer, and turned the shirt into one of the most recognisable symbols in world football. But Argentina has tried to do this before, when Diego Maradona was the player being honoured, and FIFA stopped it. More than two decades later, the same regulation stands in the way of giving Messi the ultimate tribute.Argentina wanted to retire Maradona’s No.10 tooThe idea of retiring Argentina’s No.10 is not new, and its strongest precedent comes from the country’s other footballing icon.On 25 September 2001, the Argentine Football Association voted unanimously, on the initiative of then-president Julio Grondona, to retire the No.10 shirt in honour of Maradona.The plan was to put the decision into effect before the 2002 World Cup, and at the time it appeared to be settled. Argentine newspaper Olé even ran a front-page headline declaring: "It is God's will."There was, however, one problem: FIFA had its own rules governing squad numbers at its tournaments.FIFA rejected Argentina’s request, meaning the No.10 could not simply disappear from the World Cup squad. Ariel "El Burrito" Ortega ultimately wore the shirt for Argentina at the 2002 tournament, becoming the player who wore the famous number most prominently between the Maradona and Messi eras.The significance of that episode has returned now that Messi has stepped away from the national team.This time, it is not Maradona’s name attached to the request. It is Messi’s.Why FIFA will not let Argentina retire the shirtThe obstacle is not a lack of willingness from Argentina. It is the numbering system FIFA applies to its official tournaments.According to Marca, FIFA regulations require tournament squad lists for competitions such as the World Cup and Copa America to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26. Every player selected for the 26-man squad must therefore have a number, with none omitted.That makes retiring the No.10 impossible in an official tournament.Argentina could want to leave the number untouched, supporters could overwhelmingly back the idea and the Argentine Football Association could decide that nobody should wear it again, but the regulations would still require the No.10 to be assigned to somebody when the team enters a tournament governed by FIFA's squad-number rules.In other words, Argentina cannot simply submit a 26-man squad numbered 1 through 9 and 11 through 27, or leave the No.10 blank as a permanent tribute to Messi. The numbering requirement creates a direct conflict with the idea of permanently retiring the shirt.That is exactly what happened with Maradona.The regulation therefore means Messi's No.10 can be treated differently in friendly matches, where Argentina could choose not to use the number, but the situation changes as soon as the national team enters an official tournament.Must read: Argentina ready to hand Messi’s iconic No.10 shirt to 21-year-old star if Scaloni staysMessi’s No.10 has become impossible to separate from his legacyThe desire to retire the shirt is understandable because Messi did far more than simply inherit Maradona's number.He wore No.10 for Argentina for roughly two decades and leaves the national team as its all-time leading scorer and most-capped player. His international career also transformed the meaning of the shirt for another generation of Argentine supporters, just as Maradona had done before him.That is why the debate is not really about who deserves to wear the number next. It is about whether anybody should wear it at all.The Argentine Football Association has previously expressed a clear desire to retire the shirt once Messi ended his international career.In 2024, AFA president Claudio Tapia told Sport: "The national team's number 10 shirt will be retired when Messi ends his international career."Tapia's comments made the association's intention clear, but the practical problem was always going to be FIFA's tournament regulations.The situation leaves Argentina with an unusual compromise. The No.10 could effectively be reserved as Messi's number whenever the team plays certain friendlies, allowing the association and supporters to honour him without giving the shirt to another player.But when the next World Cup or Copa America arrives, the number cannot simply be erased from Argentina's squad list.Someone will have to wear it.Must read: Argentina ready to hand Messi’s iconic No.10 shirt to 21-year-old star if Scaloni staysThe next No.10 will inherit a shirt unlike any otherThat leaves Argentina facing another difficult question: if the No.10 cannot be retired, who takes it?Messi's successor will inevitably inherit a shirt carrying the weight of both him and Maradona. It is one thing to wear the No.10 for Argentina; it is another to wear the number that has belonged to two of the country's greatest footballers.Several names could enter the conversation, including Alexis Mac Allister, Enzo Fernández, Thiago Almada and Nico Paz.According to ESPN Argentina insider Federico Bueno, Argentina have an internal plan for Paz to take the No.10 if Lionel Scaloni renews his contract as head coach, with negotiations expected to take place in the coming months.For now, though, the immediate reality is simpler: Messi's No.10 cannot be permanently removed from Argentina's official tournament squad.Maradona's Argentina tried it in 2001 and FIFA said no. More than 20 years later, the same rule means Messi's shirt faces the same fate.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Report: Lionel Messi could get one final Argentina appearance as captain in front of home fans despite retirement
articles.summary: Football News: Amidst speculation of retirement, Lionel Messi could have one last match for Argentina, allowing fans to bid farewell at home. Reports suggest the AFA may plan a special match during the next FIFA international window.
articles.body: Lionel Messi may have already played his final competitive match for Argentina, but reports suggest his farewell to the national team could still have one more chapter. Messi confirmed his retirement from international football in a lengthy post on social media, with the 2026 World Cup final against Spain expected to mark the end of his Argentina career. Yet Argentina could organise a special farewell match for their captain during the next FIFA international window. Nothing has been confirmed, and the Argentine Football Association would first need to establish whether Messi himself wants to take part, but the possibility is already being discussed. If it happens, it could give Argentina's supporters the chance to say goodbye to their greatest player on home soil.Argentina could organise Messi farewell matchAccording to reports from Argentina, the AFA is considering arranging a farewell appearance for Messi during the next FIFA international window, which runs from September 21 to October 6.The federation is expected to organise two or three friendly matches, with some reports suggesting Argentina could play as many as three or four during the window. The opponents, dates and venues have not yet been confirmed.Argentine journalist Pablo Gravellone of Todo Noticias reported that all signs point towards Messi playing his final Argentina match at home.A potential venue is Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, where Argentina regularly plays its home matches. There is also a possibility of the national team taking the occasion to Rosario, Messi's hometown, although that is considered less likely.TNT Sports Argentina's Maximiliano Grillo reported: "Argentina are working to arrange two or three friendly matches in September. The games are expected to be played in Buenos Aires, Cordoba and/or Rosario, with the opponents yet to be confirmed."That leaves plenty still to be decided.There is currently no confirmed opponent, match date or venue for a Messi farewell, and the idea remains at the reporting stage rather than an official AFA announcement.Most importantly, Argentina would first need to speak to Messi and determine whether he is willing to return for the occasion.Messi's World Cup farewell may not have been his lastThe possibility of another appearance comes only days after Messi announced his international retirement.On August 31, the Inter Miami star confirmed that he had decided to end his Argentina career after a remarkable 207-cap international career, during which he scored 125 goals and won six major titles, most notably the 2022 World Cup.His decision followed Argentina's 2026 World Cup final defeat to Spain, which appeared to bring his international career to a close.A farewell match would therefore be very different from another competitive fixture. Argentina would not be trying to give Messi one more tournament run; instead, the occasion would allow the player and supporters to formally close a chapter that ended in very different circumstances in the World Cup final.It would also allow Messi to say goodbye in front of Argentine supporters rather than ending his international career thousands of miles from home.Messi remains an active professional footballer at club level with Inter Miami, with his contract extending beyond this international retirement. That means there is no immediate issue surrounding his fitness or ability to play another match should he agree to the idea.The proposed farewell would also not necessarily resemble a traditional retirement exhibition, where former teammates and friends gather for a ceremonial game. The reports point instead towards Messi appearing for Argentina in an official international friendly, potentially wearing the captain's armband one final time.For now, though, that remains dependent on discussions that have yet to take place.Read Next: Argentina ready to hand Messi’s iconic No.10 shirt to 21-year-old star if Scaloni staysArgentina still have to decide who replaces Messi as captainWhile the possibility of one final Messi appearance is being discussed, Argentina also have to begin preparing for life without the captain who has led them through one of the most successful periods in their history.Cristian Romero appears to be one of the leading candidates to inherit the armband. The defender has already captained Argentina on several occasions when Messi was unavailable and is regarded as a natural leader within the squad.He is not the only possibility.Emiliano "Dibu" Martinez and Enzo Fernández have also been mentioned as potential successors because of their experience, importance to the team and standing within the dressing room.There is another complication, however.Nicolas Otamendi, who had generally taken the captain's armband whenever Messi was not in the starting XI, had already announced his retirement from international football immediately after the World Cup.That means Argentina enter their next era without the usual succession option that had existed behind Messi.A farewell match could therefore provide an unusual moment for the transition. Messi could potentially lead Argentina one last time before the armband officially passes to a new generation.But until the AFA confirms its plans, even that remains uncertain.And there is one more question waiting for the next generation: who wears the No.10 after Messi?Reports have suggested Nico Paz could be the preferred choice, but only if Lionel Scaloni renews his contract as Argentina head coach. That decision is expected to be discussed in the coming months, meaning even Messi's eventual successor remains tied to what happens with Scaloni.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Santos FC sign right-back Rodinei
articles.summary: Rodinei is Santos Futebol Clube’s newest signing! With a successful career in Brazil and Europe, the right-back, who had been playing for Olympiacos in Greec...
articles.body:
Rodinei is Santos Futebol Clube's newest signing! With a successful career in Brazil and Europe, the right-back, who had been playing for Olympiacos in Greece, has signed a contract with Peixe until the end of 2027.

"It is a great joy to be able to wear the shirt of a huge club like Santos FC. I'm arriving highly motivated and fully aware of the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt. I hope to deliver on the pitch and, together with my teammates, bring the fans lots of joy, because I know they deserve to smile," said Santos's new signing.

Born in Tatuí, in the interior of São Paulo state, Rodinei took his first steps in professional football with Avaí. Early in his career, he also played for Corinthians, Marcílio Dias, CRAC and Penapolense before joining Ponte Preta in 2013. At the Campinas-based club, the right-back began drawing attention for his speed, physical strength and ability to support the attack.

Those strong performances earned Rodinei a move to Flamengo in 2016. At the Rio club, he enjoyed the most successful spell of his career. In six seasons, he won two Campeonato Carioca titles, one Brazilian Championship, two Conmebol Libertadores titles and one Copa do Brasil. He also spent a period on loan at Internacional.

At the end of 2022, Rodinei began a new chapter in his career by moving to Olympiacos. He quickly established himself as one of the team's main options and won four titles, highlighted by the UEFA Conference League in the 2023/24 season, the first continental trophy in the Greek club's history.

In addition, the right-back won the Greek League (2024/25), the Greek Cup (2024/25), the Greek Super Cup (2025), and was named to the league's Team of the Season twice (2023 and 2024). He ended his spell as the second Brazilian with the most appearances in Olympiacos history, taking the field 157 times, behind only Santos idol Giovanni, who made 169 appearances.

With speed, physical strength and a constant presence in attack, the full-back now returns to Brazilian football to wear the Sacred Shirt of Santos FC. Welcome, Rodinei!

articles.title: Luka Modric talks about special bond with Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho: ‘Would do anything for him’
articles.summary: Luka Modric has revealed the extraordinary role Jose Mourinho played in bringing him to Real Madrid, with the club icon insisting that the Portuguese manager...
articles.body:
Luka Modric has revealed the extraordinary role Jose Mourinho played in bringing him to Real Madrid, with the club icon insisting that the Portuguese manager's return to the Santiago Bernabeu can restore a fearsome edge to the team .

Modric, who left Real Madrid in 2025 and turns 41 next week, spoke at length to AS about Mourinho's appointment and his own memories of the Portuguese coach.

There is clearly still a strong bond between the pair, almost 15 years after Mourinho pushed Madrid to sign the midfielder from Tottenham Hotspur.

Speaking about the manager, he believes Real Madrid made the right call by bringing Mourinho back and has already noticed a change in the team.

"You can already see from the first few matches that this is a different Real Madrid, a fearsome Real Madrid.

"I think Mourinho's appointment was a very wise decision by the club, the best option for that position considering the team and everything.

"He knows the club, he's a winner, he has an incredible personality, and I have a special affection for him because he was the one who brought me here, which was the most important factor in my arrival. He told the club: "I want him or nobody else."

Mourinho's demand changed Modric's career

Mourinho requested Luka Modric's signing from Tottenham. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images)

Modric explained that Mourinho's insistence was particularly important because negotiations with Tottenham were complicated.

"That's why I came to Real Madrid. The way the negotiations unfolded, perhaps if it hadn't been for that, Real Madrid would have withdrawn from the deal because of all the back and forth.

"That's why I have so much affection and respect for him. My only regret is not having worked with him longer."

The former midfielder also mentioned what makes Mourinho special to him, stating

"Mourinho is special to me because of how he fought for my signing; that's something you don't forget. I would do anything for him.

"Although we don't talk much, we sometimes exchange messages, but I always wish him the best.

"I think he's in the right place because he's at the best club in the world, and he's one of the best coaches in history."

Modric refuses to make Barcelona the focus

Modric was also asked whether Mourinho's return could put Barcelona under greater pressure, particularly after Barça's recent domestic success.

Modric refused to talk about the Negreira case. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

His response was typically Madrid-minded: the focus should remain on Real Madrid rather than its biggest rival.

"Real Madrid should never look at what others are doing, only at itself.

"Barcelona might be its biggest rival, but Real Madrid should be focused on its own game and let others worry about Real Madrid, not the other way around."

The former midfielder was less willing to engage in the debate surrounding refereeing and the Negreira case, although he acknowledged that the situation was not normal.

"It's a situation that really isn't normal. I'm not going to go into it any further because I don't like it."

Instead, Modric offered his explanation for why Madrid won six Champions Leagues during his career but fewer La Liga titles.

He felt the difference came partly from the mentality required by the two competitions, with Champions League mistakes immediately punished while league points could appear recoverable.

Modric also discussed Real Madrid's attacking stars, praising Vinicius Junior and Kylian Mbappe while reserving particular affection for Jude Bellingham because of the Englishman's midfield role.

"They're phenomenal. I'm so glad Vinicius renewed his contract with the club; it wouldn't have been good if he hadn't, given everything he contributes.

Modric has backed Bellingham to become Real Madrid's leader. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"Kylian is incredible: the ease with which he scores goals, his quickness and speed are spectacular. But the one I feel closest to is Jude, because he's a midfielder like me."

He also believes Bellingham has the qualities to become a leader at the Bernabéu.

"Yes, he can be a leader. The fans at the Bernabéu appreciate that he gives his all on the pitch; he gives it his absolute all. They value not just his talent, but his hard work.

"What he did at the World Cup and how he's started this year is incredible; I hope he carries on like this."

Meanwhile, Modric declined to pick a Ballon d'Or winner, saying the decision belongs to the voters.

But when asked about a possible return to Real Madrid after retirement, his answer was much more definitive.

"I hope it happens. Madrid is my home and always will be. I'll always be a Madridista because of everything I experienced there.

"They were the best years of my professional and personal life. I hope I can return one day, but we'll have to see in what capacity," he concluded.

articles.title: Lautaro Martinez finally breaks his silence on Barcelona links: ‘My only clear desire is…’
articles.summary: Lautaro Martinez has made his position clear on Barcelona links, with the Inter Milan captain confirming that he wants to remain at San Siro despite the summ...
articles.body:
Lautaro Martinez has made his position clear on Barcelona links, with the Inter Milan captain confirming that he wants to remain at San Siro despite the summer transfer speculation linking him with a move to Catalonia.

It must be remembered that Barcelona explored alternatives after their pursuit of Julian Alvarez failed to materialise, and Lautaro emerged as one of the forwards considered by the club.

The Argentine's name featured prominently in reports during the transfer window, with claims that Barça had begun laying the groundwork for a possible deal.

Those reports suggested Barcelona sporting director Deco and Bojan Krkic had met Lautaro's representative in Madrid and discussed the player's potential contract.

There was even speculation that personal terms had been agreed , leaving Barcelona needing to negotiate only with Inter should they decide to push ahead.

Barcelona were tracking Lautaro Martinez during the transfer window. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

But the biggest obstacle was never Lautaro himself. Inter had little appetite for losing their captain.

Inter Milan never wanted to sell Lautaro

Barcelona were believed to be considering an opening offer below €100 million . That scenario ultimately never developed.

Inter president Giuseppe Marotta made the Italian club's position unmistakable when asked about the possibility of Lautaro leaving.

"I can say explicitly that there are absolutely no conditions for him to leave Inter."

That stance was important because, while Lautaro was clearly a player Barcelona had considered, Inter's resistance meant any serious transfer would have required a major change in the Italian club's position.

Lautaro Martinez ends Barcelona speculation

Inter Milan never wanted to sell Lautaro. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Now, it is Lautaro himself who has provided the clearest answer yet.

As reported by Fabrizio Romano , the Inter forward admitted that the Barcelona links were flattering but insisted that his priority was never to force a move away from Milan.

"Barcelona links made me proud, but I want to stay here. My only clear desire is to stay at Inter.

"I love this club, I love these people, I love the fans. I will stay here as long as they want me," he concluded.

articles.title: La plantilla del Athletic mira a Uriarte...y éste a los expresidentes
articles.standfirst: Los capitanes del equipo están pendientes de la reunión pactada con el dirigente
articles.summary: Los capitanes del equipo están pendientes de la reunión pactada con el dirigente
articles.body: La atención en el Athletic va más allá de lo que pueda ofrecer el partido de este sábado ante el Atlético, segundo de la temporada en San Mamés para los de Terzic. Los puntos de la victoria de Vigo, con un muy buen juego en la primera mitad, alimentan las buenas sensaciones deportivas. Pero éstas se cruzan con la marejada institucional, con los futbolistas frente a la directiva y los expresidentes también alterados por las decisiones y la trascendencia que han tomado las decisiones de Jon Uriarte. La primera plantilla mira al presidente, con el que tienen pactada una reunión que todavía no se ha producido. Los futbolistas pensaban haberse reunido antes del partido ante el Barcelona, pero al no recibir respuesta ni comunicación alguna al respecto decidieron no realizar declaraciones ante los medios de comunicación, circunstancia que penalizará el bonus de la Liga al finalizar la temporada. “Fue una herramienta para dar una señal a la directiva y el presidente”, explicó Simón al término del partido ante el Celta. “Y funcionó”, agregó. Esta semana los capitanes y el dirigente del club deben tratar el desencuentro. “Son pequeños detalles que se han ido haciendo bola durante estos cuatro años”, resumió Simón. Uriarte, que no acompañó al equipo ni a Barcelona ni a Vigo, tiene en su mano que la plantilla no recupere sus “herramientas” para dar señales en caso de que el presidente excuse el encuentro. Si los futbolistas miran al presidente, éste debería hacerlo con los ex presidentes, aunque Uriarte no se ha destacado por una gran relación con sus antecesores. Los expresidentes del club, a excepción de Josu Urrutia, se reunirán este jueves para abordar diversos asuntos de una actualidad rojiblanca que ha trascendido hacia el exterior y que pone a varios colectivos de uñas. Una de las preocupaciones de los asistentes es el delicado lugar al que puede derivar la institucionalidad del club. Aitor Elizegi, el anterior presidente a Uriarte, aprovechó sus redes sociales para expresar que "hace años que nos reunimos, suele ser varias veces al año y habrá más. Debería ser normal y recomendable, de manera periódica, para quien le interese y a poder ser en sede oficial, sin niguna relevancia, en algún rincón que tenga el Club, si hace falta llevo el café". El expresidente destacó lo grato de esos encuentros, que siempre provocan debate entre los asistentes, y respecto a la polémica de las invitaciones fue claro: "a mí no me tiene que invitar nadie a San Mamés, voy hace 30 años por mi cuenta a mi localidad. Pensaba que el Club reconocía un trabajo y una dedicación. Supongo que para algunos no habrá sido suficiente, son los nuevos tiempos".

articles.title: Las plusvalías pendientes pasan factura al mercado del Betis
articles.standfirst: El club ha invertido unos 30 millones en fichajes, casi lo mismo que ha ingresado en ventas
articles.summary: El club ha invertido unos 30 millones en fichajes, casi lo mismo que ha ingresado en ventas
articles.body: El Betis ha cerrado un mercado de fichajes que ha dejado cierta frustración entre sus aficionados. La plantilla mantiene buena parte del bloque que logró la clasificación para la Champions, incluidas sus principales estrellas (Antony, Abde, Cucho, Fornals, Isco, Natan...) y ha incorporado futbolistas importantes, con Dani Ceballos como guinda en el último día, pero la renovación no ha podido ser tan profunda como inicialmente se pretendía. Pellegrini puede echar en falta la llegada de un centrocampista de corte posicional, puesto en el que, como reclamó públicamente, le faltaba una pieza, pese a que la Dirección Deportiva entendiera que una nueva incorporación podía restar oportunidades a su gran apuesta, Facundo Bernal. Y también se echa en falta un central que pudiera elevar el nivel competitivo de esa demarcación, al tiempo que sobran centrocampistas después de que ni Iker Losada ni Nelson Deossa ni Álvaro Fidalgo atendieran las propuestas que tenían para salir. Detrás de buena parte de las dificultades que ha encontrado el club para completar su planificación aparece una cuestión económica que su presidente, Ángel Haro, trató de explicar ayer tras la presentación de Parrott y Ceballos como nuevos jugadores del Betis, en una extensa rueda de prensa, junto a Manu Fajardo, en la que llevó a cabo un detallado balance del mercado: la necesidad de generar plusvalías para sostener el elevado coste de la plantilla. El presidente utilizó como argumento que "el Betis es el cuarto equipo que más ha invertido en esta temporada de fichajes y tiene la quinta mayor plantilla de LaLiga". Una inversión que ronda los 30 millones de euros más variables por objetivos. Aunque el dato necesita también su contexto porque el club este verano, con las ventas de Sergi Altimira, Nobel Mendy (primero al Rayo y luego un porcentaje más con su marcha al Hull City) y Pablo García ha recaudado una cantidad prácticamente equivalente. El problema, por tanto, no está tanto en el balance directo entre compras y ventas de esta ventana veraniega de transferencias como en las necesidades económicas que arrastra el Betis y en el coste de la plantilla que pretende mantener: "El Betis tiene unos gastos ordinarios, formados por la plantilla deportiva, y con nuestros ingresos ordinarios no es suficiente. Hay que tener plusvalías para poder cuadrar las cuentas si queremos tener esta plantilla", reconoció Haro. Una situación que viene condicionada también por el ejercicio anterior. El club heliopolitano cerró la pasada temporada sin conseguir todas las plusvalías que había presupuestado, una desviación que ha reducido su margen de maniobra y que explica algunas de las particularidades del mercado recién finalizado. Haro detalló además por qué una operación como el traspaso de Pablo García al Racing, cerrada en las últimas horas, no proporcionó al Betis nuevo margen para reforzar inmediatamente la plantilla. "Incluso la plusvalía que se ha producido tampoco afecta al límite, teniendo en cuenta que tienes un límite donde hay una plusvalía estimada en función de la media de los últimos tres años, y hasta que no llegues a esa cantidad cualquier plusvalía no te computa", dijo. Es decir, parte de las plusvalías que vaya generando el Betis sirven primero para cubrir las cantidades ya contempladas en sus previsiones económicas antes de proporcionar margen adicional en el límite de coste de plantilla. De ahí que la operación de Pablo García tampoco fuera necesaria para poder cerrar la llegada de Ceballos. "Por tanto, desde un punto de vista ni deportivo ni económico afectaba a la llegada de Dani Ceballos. De alguna manera se ha ido comentando que era necesaria la salida de Pablo para la llegada de Dani y es algo totalmente falso", insistió Haro. La inscripción del utrerano sí ha obligado, sin embargo, al Betis a asumir un esfuerzo adicional en sus cuentas después de que no se produjeran varias de las salidas con las que trabajaba la Dirección Deportiva. "El esfuerzo es fundamentalmente un esfuerzo en la cuenta de resultados. Tendrían que haberse producido algunas de las salidas para que no fuera tal esfuerzo; no se produjeron esas salidas que esperábamos días antes del cierre del mercado y por tanto las plusvalías que tenemos que generar este año para cuadrar cuentas son mayores", explicó el presidente. Ahí aparece una de las principales consecuencias del mercado. El Betis ha conseguido encajar a Ceballos sin desprenderse de ninguno de sus principales activos, pero a cambio eleva la cantidad de plusvalías que deberá generar durante el ejercicio 2026-27. Es decir, ya sea en el próximo mercado invernal, en enero, o el próximo verano, a ser posible antes del cierre del ejercicio a 30 de junio, los verdiblancos necesitan generar plusvalías para evitar el desfase. El club tuvo la posibilidad de avanzar buena parte de ese camino el último día de mercado con Abde. Llegó una importante propuesta por el internacional marroquí, procedente del Everton, pero a esas alturas del verano el Betis sólo estaba dispuesto a aceptar una cantidad prácticamente irrechazable: "Llegó una oportunidad de gran venta con la operación de Abde el último día de mercado, pero entendíamos que ese día había que pedir prácticamente la cláusula; no se llegó a la cláusula y decidimos mantener la plantilla en un año de Champions". La consecuencia deportiva de todo este escenario es que la planificación terminó sin poder completar algunos de los movimientos que se habían manejado. Especialmente significativo fue el del pivote defensivo. Pellegrini había solicitado públicamente un jugador de ese perfil y el Betis llegó al último día de mercado valorando esa incorporación e incluso sondeando varios nombres por si una salida de última hora abría la puerta a un fichaje con el que poner el broche a la planificación, pero dichas salidas necesarias no se produjeron. Manu Fajardo defiende ahora que la apuesta del club para esa posición es Facundo Bernal, acompañado por Marc Roca, aunque admite que el escenario podría haber sido distinto con alguna ficha disponible: "Tenemos jugadores en la plantilla que pueden ocupar esa demarcación y no se sabe si, de haber tenido fichas disponibles, hubiésemos ido a por un perfil más defensivo o de mayor equilibrio". El propio director deportivo realizó autocrítica precisamente por las dificultades para aligerar la plantilla. "A la hora de dar salidas a jugadores, hay que afrontarlo desde una postura o dureza que a lo mejor no hemos tenido en distintos momentos del mercado; de eso se aprende". El escenario económico obliga así al Betis a mantener un complicado equilibrio entre sus aspiraciones deportivas y su capacidad de generar recursos. Haro puso cifras a esa elección. Según el presidente, el club podría prescindir de la necesidad recurrente de plusvalías, pero tendría que reducir de forma importante su inversión en la plantilla: "Puedes plantearte que no sean necesarias las plusvalías para cuadrar cuentas, pero eso conlleva que en lugar de tener 140 millones de gastos de plantilla deportiva, te tienes que ir probablemente a 105. Eso significa competir con equipos que suelen estar entre el puesto 8 y el 12". El Betis, a la espera del nuevo Benito Villamarín que aumente los ingresos recurrentes y reduzca la necesidad de realizar este tipo de ventas, ha optado durante los últimos años por mantener el primero de esos modelos, más exigente económicamente y apoyado en la generación recurrente de plusvalías. Una fórmula que ha acompañado al crecimiento deportivo del equipo, pero que este verano, después de no alcanzar los traspasos previstos en el ejercicio anterior y de no conseguir algunas de las salidas esperadas, ha terminado condicionando la profundidad de la renovación de una plantilla que afronta el regreso a la Champions con jugadores de muchísimo nivel, pero con algunas incógnitas sobre las que el tiempo terminará dictando sentencia.

articles.title: The rise and fall of Schalke, Germany's fallen giants
articles.summary: One of Germany's fallen giants, Schalke are back in the Bundesliga after a complicated few years.
articles.body:
On matchday, even for friendlies, Gelsenkirchen pauses as locals turn their attention to Schalke's Veltins-Arena.

Everywhere you look, swathes of fans in blue and white are arriving by tram, on foot or by car.

In the team's first game back in the Bundesliga for three years, 6,000 away fans stayed after the final whistle to support the players despite a 3-0 defeat at Augsburg.

"It's a kind of religious feeling that people have towards Schalke," said Professor Frank Eckardt, who grew up in the Schalke-Nord area.

"It feels like people think, 'OK, we don't have anything else, but we have Schalke. It's our club.'

"If you go to graveyards, for example, you will find that people have Schalke on their graves in one way or the other. So it is really something deep.

"You can take everything from us, but you will never take Schalke from us. That's what they really believe."

Alvarez to Arsenal? Plus Muslić on Schalke

Listen to the More than the Score podcast

When Schalke fell to Bundesliga 2 for the first time in 21 years and insolvency looked a genuine possibility - because of massive debts brought on by rash spending, failure to qualify for Europe and Covid-19 - the only guarantee was the fans would remain.

Despite the threat against the club's existence, Schalke bounced back to the top flight straight away in 2022.

A year later they were in the second tier again, and that is where they would stay for the next three seasons, with the first two campaigns showing little hope for the future.

A 10th-placed finish was followed by an even more dismal 14th - only two places above a relegation play-off spot.

German football expert Mark Lovell said: "They suffered with the burden of expectation. They were expected to basically walk the league every season despite having huge financial problems.

"There's sympathy for Schalke, but they've been their own worst enemies by chasing success and extending themselves too far.

"They've been living beyond their means for many seasons. When you do suffer relegation something has to give, and they haven't been able to buy their way out.

"They had to live more to their needs and get rid of their best players, and then sort of start again with a real skeleton type operation."

After finishing 14th, new figures were brought in - including former Plymouth Argyle manager Miron Muslic - who helped build Schalke's promotion to the Bundesliga last year.

Robin Haack, who covers Schalke for local newspaper WAV, said: "He is the face of the Schalke promotion.

"He is the hero because his way of coaching is so powerful. He gave the people the belief back.

"Nobody knew him before. Some Austrian who was relegated to the third league in England - he must be bad.

"But he proved all the haters wrong in an incredible way. Fans love him like I've never experienced a coach has been loved before."

Muslic operates with a high-press style and has created a team that represent Gelsenkirchen's working-class nature with committment and effort.

"Muslic was the perfect match," said Haack.

If Muslic was the cover star, working behind the scenes was former director of football at Werder Bremen and Germany international Frank Baumann, who joined Schalke in June 2025.

Andreas Ernst, who also reports for WAV, said: "He had the whole club, but it lay on the ground.

"They said do whatever you want to do. But with no money. We have a bad team. But come here - a very great club.

"Frank Baumann did everything out of nothing."

Lovell said: "At Schalke right now there's some very intelligent football people behind the scenes.

"Frank Baumann's a real top football man, and just a decent person, which Schalke didn't have."

Baumann's most eye-catching signing was former Manchester City forward Edin Dzeko, who joined in January after a torrid spell in Italy with Fiorentina.

He has scored eight goals in 13 games, including two this season in Schalke's DFB Pokal cup win.

Muslic told BBC's Euro Leagues podcast: "I grew up in Austria, but I'm from Bosnia. And Edin Dzeko for us is Gary Lineker. He's our Johan Cruyff. He's our Franz Beckenbauer. He's just an idol.

"He's 40 years old, and he's still able to perform. That means he was super professional the last 25 years.

"That's why he's a role model and that's why he will also have his impact and he will leave also his fingerprints in this upcoming Bundesliga season."

With his experience at top-flight clubs across Europe, Dzeko's will also offer something invaluable to Muslic's team.

Schalke defender Christian Fuchs told BBC's More Than The Score podcast: "Where it's a player like this... there's so much respect towards him from his team-mates.

"It's so important to build a club culture, to hold players accountable, to keep them all in check.

"Even if it's a small piece in the bigger puzzle, there is so much value that you need to give to that.

"Dzeko plays an important part in growing stability in the club."

Dzeko had been established with every club he has played for, but for others they have had to rebuild their careers with Schalke.

Former Liverpool goalkeeper Loris Karius has questioned multiple times whether to end his career, but has managed to regain a starting spot and become a key figure in Muslic's team.

Muslic said: "He is the face of this new Schalke, the face of this new resilience, this new mindset.

"After tough years behind him, he found a new home. He found new trust - like so many other players from Schalke who had some rough moments in their careers.

"They found a safe heaven. And then it was just about, let's do this together and let's start from scratch and let's do it in our way."

Schalke will need to showcase this new mentality against champions Bayern Munich in their first home game of the season on Saturday, after the Augsburg defeat.

This match will not define Schalke's season. Neither will the fierce rivalry with Borussia Dortmund. Instead, it will be shaped by every game at the Veltins-Arena, which will be packed with 62,000 passionate fans.

Fuchs said: "I know Dortmund. They don't admit it, but I'm sure they miss Schalke.

"Schalke is just a club that in my eyes belong into the Bundesliga and I hope... we'll see them there for a very long time."

Many Schalke fans do not have high expectations this season, with some saying they simply need to avoid relegation.

Muslic said: "We know the glory of the past. But we know also the present and the future.

"We are very humble but ambitious. Right now it's all about playing another year in the Bundesliga."

articles.title: Rayane Belaid firma cinco años con el Rayo Vallecano
articles.standfirst: El conjunto vallecano oficializa el traspaso del canterano del Atlético de Madrid
articles.summary: Medidapunta
articles.body: Rayane Belaid, nuevo jugador del Rayo Vallecano: cinco años para el mediapunta del Atlético Madrileño, que administrativamente tendrá ficha del Rayo C, pero será jugador de la dinámica del equipo de Beñat San José. El Rayo Vallecano ya tiene nuevo refuerzo para su centro del campo. El club franjirrojo ha anunciado el acuerdo con el Atlético de Madrid para el traspaso definitivo de Rayane Belaid Khelil, que firma por cinco temporadas. El futbolista, nacido en Orihuela, destaca por aportar talento, creatividad y desequilibrio en la zona de tres cuartos. Belaid nació el 11 de febrero de 2005 en Orihuela (Alicante) y tiene 21 años. Es un mediapunta, aunque también puede actuar como centrocampista ofensivo. Su trayectoria está ligada al Atlético de Madrid. Se formó en su cantera, pasó por el Juvenil A y dio el salto al filial, el Atlético Madrileño. La pasada temporada también tuvo presencia en el primer equipo, con el que debutó en LaLiga en abril de 2026. En la temporada 2025-26, Belaid disputó 31 partidos de Primera Federación con el Atlético Madrileño, 22 como titular, y marcó cuatro goles. Además, jugó dos encuentros de LaLiga con el primer equipo rojiblanco, en los que acumuló 134 minutos, sin goles ni asistencias. Internacional con las categorías inferiores de España, fue campeón de Europa Sub-19 en 2024 y posteriormente jugó con la Sub-20, incluido el Mundial de la categoría. Su estreno con el Atlético en LaLiga llegó en abril de 2026, un paso importante antes de afrontar ahora su primera etapa como jugador del Rayo. El conjunto vallecano incorpora así a un futbolista de presente y proyección, con experiencia en el fútbol profesional y formado en una de las canteras más reconocidas de España.

articles.title: Celtic transfer news: Martin O'Neill's Hoops add SIX ahead of UEFA deadline but will more follow?
articles.summary: The Scottish champions signed six players ahead of the European deadline; they came after they failed to reach the Champions League; Martin O'Neill has made 10 summer signings so far; watch St Mirren vs Celtic on Saturday, live on Sky Sports from 7.30pm
articles.body:
The Hoops brought in four loan players ahead of their 3-0 win over Aberdeen and confirmed the arrivals of 19-year-old midfielder Joel van den Berg from PSV Eindhoven and Swiss right-back Jordan Lotomba soon after the game.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen and Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka made their debuts off the bench in the Scottish Premiership clash.

Wolves goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was also among the substitutes while a second 18-year-old Chelsea player, left-back Landon Emenalo, also signed but is several weeks away from fitness.

Van den Berg then arrived on a four-year deal while 27-year-old Lotomba has signed until the end of the season.

Both signings were completed just ahead of the UEFA registration deadline of 11pm on Wednesday.

But, with limited space for overseas players in their Europa League squad, Celtic could make further signings before the Scottish Premiership deadline of 5pm on Thursday.

The Hoops have been linked with a move for Torino midfielder Gvidas Gineitis.

Celtic freed up further space in their squad on Tuesday night with the permanent departures of Johnny Kenny and Reo Hatate to Preston and Burnley respectively.

Speaking after the win over the Dons, manager Martin O'Neill said of Celtic's late arrivals: "I'm very pleased that they're in the door. I think that they'll definitely add something to us.

"Honestly I am pleased, the transfer window is there and I'm pleased that we have done what we have because there's quite a few who have left the football club.

"Reo's gone and Johnny Kenny has gone, I wish them all the best and so we need people in. Even if they miss the European deadline, if there is a possibility of getting someone else in, I would definitely want to do that if we can."

The six new arrivals in September follow the earlier summer signings of Camilo Duran, Kasper Hogh, Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan.

El equipo dirigido por José Mourinho evidenció una notable mejoría colectiva y una gran solidez defensiva, liderado por un Jude Bellingham en estado de gracia y la eficacia goleadora de Kylian Mbappé. El conjunto de Manuel Pellegrini, que había firmado un gran arranque liguero dejando la portería a cero en las dos primeras jornadas, confía en el liderazgo de veteranos como Marc Bartra para corregir los errores puntuales y mostrar su versión más competitiva. articles.body: Erling Haaland, estrella del City, tuvo una comentada reacción tras oficializar el club de Mánchester el fichaje de Enzo Fernández a cambio de 145 millones de euros. "Sí, bueno, ahora me puedo ir a la cama", publicó el delantero noruego en sus redes sociales tras confirmarse el traspaso del argentino desde el Chelsea al Manchester City. El Manchester City le pagó 145 millones de euros al Chelsea por el traspaso de Enzo Fernándeez, igualando los 145 millones de euros que el Liverpool pagó el pasado verano al Newcastle por Alexander Isak. "Todo jugador quiere ser parte de un club como este porque todo el mundo sabe lo bien dirigido que está el City", dijo el argentino en declaraciones a los medios del City. "No podría estar más feliz de estar aquí y estoy listo para el resto de ayudar al City a seguir ganando títulos. Este es un club hecho para ganar. Si miras a la plantilla, el City tiene calidad en todas las posiciones. Quiero aprender de mis compañeros y ser mejor jugador... Me enorgullece mucho seguir mejorando mi juego. Cualquiera que haya entrenador conmigo sabe lo duro que trabajo cada día y lo que pongo en cada partido. Lo doy todo y puedo prometer a este club que eso seguirá así", compartió Enzo Fernández.

articles.title: Caso Negreira: ¿Sentencia para finales de 2027?
articles.standfirst: La previsión es que la instrucción se cierre a final de 2026 y se señale el juicio para el próximo
articles.summary: La previsión es que la instrucción se cierre a final de 2026 y se señale el juicio para el próximo
articles.body: La jueza del caso Negreira decidió esta semana no admitir la petición del Real Madrid para que se extendiera la instrucción del caso durante seis meses más. El club blanco pretendía buscar más pruebas ante los indicios de un supuesto delito de corrupción deportiva, pero la jueza considera que no es necesario y que ya es suficiente con el actual periodo de instrucción. Se realizarán las diligencias pendientes que están previstas, como la declaración de Gerard López el próximo mes de noviembre, y ya está. El Real Madrid puede recurrir a la Audiencia, pero todo hace indicar que la instrucción ha finalizado definitivamente. ¿Y ahora qué? Pues todo se encamina hacia la celebración del juicio y el anuncio de una sentencia que todo el mundo del fútbol espera desde hace tres años y medio. Todas las diligencias pendientes y los recursos deberían estar resueltos antes de final de año. A partir de ese momento, las dos partes tendrían que presentar sus escritos de conclusiones, primero la acusación y luego la defensa. Y con ello se cerraría la instrucción. El caso pasaría al juzgado de lo penal si debe producirse el juicio. Aquí es donde se puede retrasar el proceso, porque depende del juzgado en el que recaiga. Hay algunos que están más saturados que otros. Sin embargo, lo más normal es que se fijara una fecha para el juicio para otoño de 2027. Antes parece muy justo para que pueda celebrarse. Y si tuviera lugar en octubre o noviembre, el juicio duraría entre una y dos semanas, por lo que nos podemos encontrar con que la sentencia del caso Negreira se podría anunciar antes de que finalice 2027. Las fechas de todo el proceso, de aquí hasta la sentencia, pueden variar por múltiples factores, pero fuentes jurídicas consultadas por MARCA indican que este podría ser el 'timing' para que hubiera una sentencia a finales del año que viene.

articles.body: El marroquí Ez Abde ha sido la principal ausencia en el entrenamiento del Betis de este jueves, último de los de Pellegrini antes de recibir mañana al Real Madrid en el Estadio de La Cartuja, en el partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de LaLiga EA Sports. Y también con una segunda jornada de trabajo con sus nuevos compañeros para Dani Ceballos, presentado ayer en el comienzo de su segunda etapa como jugador del Betis, y que pese a reconocer no encontrarse aún al 100% al no haber realizado pretemporada, se puso a las órdenes de Pellegrini por si quiere contar con él para mañana. articles.title: Fofana se estrena el una sesión de entrenamiento sin Vargas
articles.standfirst: El suizo. ausente por unas molestias sufridas en una rodilla en la jornada de trabajo de ayer
articles.summary: El suizo. ausente por unas molestias sufridas en una rodilla en la jornada de trabajo de ayer
articles.body: Con el mercado ya cerrado y sus tres últimos fichajes sobre el césped, el Sevilla, con Luis García Plaza al frente, se ha ejercitado este jueves en sus instalaciones de estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán para seguir preparando su visita del próximo domingo al Espanyol, en la cuarta jornada de LaLiga EA Sports. Una jornada de trabajo en la que la principal novedad ha sido la presencia de su último fichaje, Youssouf Fofana. El centrocampista francés, la guinda del mercado de José Ignacio Navarro, aterrizó ayer por la tarde en la capital hispalense y esta misma mañana se ha calzado las botas para conocer a sus nuevos compañeros y ponerse a disposición de su técnico. Su incorporación en calidad de cedido en las horas finales de la ventana de transferencias, aprovechando que el acuerdo para su marcha al Olympique de Lyon no se pudo concretar por problemas económicos, permitirá al Sevilla sumar una importante pieza más a la medular. Félix Correia y Lucas Stassin, los otros dos jugadores que el Sevilla incorporó en las 48 horas finales del mercado, ya trabajaron ayer con el grupo y hoy han repetido, listos para entrar en su primera convocatoria como nervionenses. Quien es duda para estar ante el Espanyol es el suizo Rubén Vargas, ausente en la sesión de entrenamiento de hoy debido a unas molestias en la rodilla que sufrió en el día de ayer, tal y como trasladan fuentes del club. El Sevilla informa que el futbolista realizó trabajo individual para regular cargas.

articles.title: Liverpool's first transfer window under Andoni Iraola sees Bradley Barcola sign but this squad is still not balanced
articles.summary: Liverpool continued to invest heavily during the summer transfer window, but Andoni Iraola’s squad still looks imbalanced despite the arrival of Bradley Barcola in the Premier League, argues Adam Bate. He analyses the personnel and structural issues at Anfield
articles.body:
"It does not look like a balanced squad," Jamie Carragher told Sky Sports . "Liverpool are short in the full-back areas and probably a midfield player as well." A succinct summary of the concerns despite the £123m signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

Even that acquisition touches upon that same issue of balance. Liverpool lost the best left-footed right-winger in Premier League history in Mohamed Salah and have responded by loading up on the mirror opposite for what looks like a lop-sided attack.

"Liverpool have not got a real out-and-out right-sided attacker," Carragher explained. "We have not got anybody with a left foot on that right side, like Mo Salah. I am disappointed. I am not quite sure what we are going to do on that right wing right now."

In truth, Barcola is versatile. But the fee surely demands him in his best position and it would be a stretch to suggest that is on the right. Cody Gakpo has been on the left flank thus far, a slot that Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike have previously been deployed in too.

There is Rio Ngumoha who enjoyed his breakthrough season on the left but has been used on the other wing in pre-season. Victor Munoz seems the most likely but he was signed off the back of one season playing in the top flight as, you guessed it, a left winger.

None of this alone is enough to damn Liverpool's recruitment strategy. It is more curiosity than catastrophe. But the worry for the supporters is that there are holes elsewhere. As a result, this seems like a squad loaded in some areas while sorely lacking in others.

When Jeremie Frimpong was signed last summer, the club were keen to stress that he was not seen as a replacement for Trent Alexander-Arnold at right-back. And yet, that is precisely where the Netherlands international has been played in the first two games.

Frimpong is the closest thing to a fit specialist in the role with Conor Bradley injured. Some make the case for Dominik Szoboszlai but that feels like a compromise. Shifting a centre-back out there is not ideal given the importance of the full-backs in Iraola's system.

That is shown by Frimpong and Milos Kerkez both ranking among the top three players in the Premier League this season for sprints. The one man above them, tellingly, is Adrien Truffert of Iraola's former club Bournemouth. This is fundamental to Iraola's approach.

Look at the average positions of Liverpool's players in their opening two matches of the campaign compared to that title-winning season under Arne Slot. The full-backs bomb on, often simultaneously, and that puts an onus on the midfielders to cover.

For Liverpool, that really could be a problem. Ryan Gravenberch famously stepped up to help Slot win that title but with Alexis Mac Allister's diminished physicality evident over the past 18 months, does Iraola have the players available to stop the counter-attacks?

Is it even his plan to use a true holding midfielder? At Bournemouth, Iraola wanted them to engage. Alex Scott talked of being "very aggressive" out of possession. "The players really believe that we are going to win the ball high up the field," said Tyler Adams.

There have already been signs that this could be a problem. "I do not believe that midfield can function with the personnel in there," said Carragher. "For me, it does not work. And it is not just about personnel, it is the structure the manager is asking for."

Within five minutes of the first Premier League game of the season, Liverpool's rest defence was exposed. With the full-backs high and the centre-backs deep, there was no midfielder in the space between them. Newcastle were able to exploit that to score.

Given the nature of Liverpool's full-backs and Virgil van Dijk's increasing inclination to retreat , it is an issue that is unlikely to go away. All of which leaves Iraola with the club's most expensively assembled squad ever - and its most obviously flawed in a decade.

Is there a solution outside of the market? To do that, compromises will be required. "You do not want to lose the offensive side, the fluidity, the arrivals with numbers, but obviously we were punished the other day, especially in the first goal," said Carragher.

"We did not do a proper lockdown. But there is a balance. We cannot go from one way where we send a lot of people forward to keeping everyone back so we do not arrive with numbers. I do not want to tell Ryan Gravenberch not to carry the ball or arrive in the box.

"It is a matter of identifying the situation. You cannot be with the joystick every time [controlling] the player. There are players that are very good at smelling the danger. 'I cannot risk going now. I think I have to stay.' Recognising those situations is the job."

For now, a couple of high-scoring draws feels about right for this Liverpool team. It remains to be seen whether their strengths will see them overpower opponents or their weaknesses will undermine them. An imbalanced, imperfect team, then. But an exciting one.
